I1.quote: Searched the full text (main article only; no supplementary file) for any gravimetric, volumetric (Sieverts) or flow measurement of H2 uptake, an adsorbed amount, wt%, mmol/g or an adsorption isotherm of this paper's own. Found none. The only measurements are QENS (T = 5, 15, 25 K) and INS (T = 1.5 K) neutron spectra; H2 was loaded by condensing 'normal H2 (75% ortho, 25% para) ... at T = 25 K and P = 1 bar into an annular-geometry aluminum cell', with no uptake quantity reported. Isotherms are mentioned only from earlier work (Tanaka et al., ref. [8]).

I5.quote: The effects of confining molecular hydrogen within carbon nanohorns are studied via high-resolution quasielastic and inelastic neutron spectroscopies.

notes: Original neutron-spectroscopy letter (QENS and INS of H2 on single-walled carbon nanohorns from MER Corporation); it has data, so not_primary does not apply. record.json is_retracted is false and no retraction notice appears in the text. It reports no experimental H2 uptake (no gravimetric, volumetric or flow value) and no surface-area measurement of its own (an area 'approaching 1500 m2 g-1' is quoted from ref. [5] as a general property of nanohorns). Not computational-only and not electrochemical, so the I1 failure is coded no_conditions_stated per the instruction. Checked page images main-01, main-09 and main-12 (abstract, Fig. 1, Fig. 4); figures are QENS and INS spectra, not uptake data.
